ansatz: tabu/greedy local search minimising monochromatic-Schur-triple count, incremental conflict tracking
why_failed: first version had a real bug: elem_tr incidence list appended a triple's index twice whenever x=y (the doubling case x+x=2x, since the loop appended once for x and once for y with x==y), double-counting that triple's delta and letting the tracked conflict count drift to a false 0 while a genuine monochromatic triple still existed. Caught by the frozen checker rejecting a witness that the incremental tracker had certified as 0-conflict (r=4,n=44: checker found 2+13=15 monochromatic in colour 1). Patched the incidence-list construction to dedupe via a set, and added a from-scratch recheck before declaring 0 -- but the recheck STILL fires after the patch (r=3,n=13 and other seeds: tracker says 0, full recompute finds 1-4 real conflicts), meaning a second, unlocated bug remains. Did not chase it further given time budget; the script now discards any spurious 0 automatically (verified: it never emits a witness the checker rejects) but is otherwise unreliable/unvalidated as a search method, so it was not used to attack the real n=536 target.
cost: ~30s across 4 runs (n=13 x3 seeds, n=44 x1), single core; bug diagnosis ~5 min

ansatz: N/A -- statement/checker mismatch, not a search failure
why_failed: the frozen check_schur_lower.py implements the STANDARD Schur condition (x=y allowed, i.e. it rejects any monochromatic doubling x+x=2x). The weak Schur number WS(6) is defined by the WEAK condition (x<y<z strict, doublings allowed). These are different forbidden-pattern sets, and the weak Schur numbers are provably >= the standard ones because the weak constraint is strictly looser. Demonstrated concretely: colouring=[0,0] (r=1,n=2) is a valid weak-Schur witness for the known exact value WS(1)=2, but the frozen checker REJECTs it (monochromatic 1+1=2). No amount of search against this checker can produce a certified weak-Schur result; the checker would have to be extended (out of write-scope: mine/verify/ is frozen) or a separate weak-Schur checker built and frozen through the proper pipeline stage. No search was run against the n=646 target for this reason.
cost: 0 (single checker invocation, <1s, to produce the demonstration)

ansatz: brute-force over the complete x-range n/4<x<=3n/4, sufficient e|(nx) divisibility test with a 1/w->1/(w+1)+1/(w(w+1)) split for a 3rd term
why_failed: never fires for n = 1 (mod 4) (empirically confirmed on all n<5000); the fully general divisor-pair completion for that residue class is only ~O(n) per n in the worst case, capping the fully-verified frontier at N=10000 (52s for the n=1 mod4 residue alone), 13 orders of magnitude short of the published N=10^17 sieve which relies on covering congruences we did not implement

ansatz: incremental exact factorial (running product) + gmpy2.isqrt exact perfect-square check per n
why_failed: big-integer multiplication cost grows faster than linearly as n! gains digits, so wall time scales superlinearly (8.44s to n=20000, 103.44s to n=60000); this naive approach cannot approach the published N=10^9 frontier, which almost certainly filters n via modular quadratic-residue sieving before ever forming n! for a survivor -- the wrong bottleneck to be fighting with more brute force

ansatz: numpy divisor-count sieve (tau[d::d]+=1 for d=1..N) with running max of m+tau(m), pure per-d Python outer loop
why_failed: outer loop over d is O(N) unvectorized Python regardless of the vectorized inner slice op, capping N at ~10^7 in the time available (10^8 timed out at 120s) -- a C-level or fully-vectorized (e.g. sieve-of-multiples via cumulative bincount) sieve is needed to close more of the gap to the kernel-checked N=10^9 published frontier
